title: RiverMark Design — PLG sprint: hosting path decision
summary: Intro discovery for RiverMark's PLG sprint. Agreed next steps: grant credits, schedule SE deep-dive, and run a 2-week hosted pilot with baseline scripts. SE to share SOC2 and KMS notes.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE); Elliot Nguyen (RiverMark CTO); Priya Sharma (Lead ML Eng); Marco Ruiz (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Customer is evaluating Redwood for a design assistant within their product. Focus on PLG/self-serve time-to-first-token, but clear enterprise constraints (VPC and KMS) are on the roadmap.

Topics: PLG quickstart, credits, hosted vs dedicated vs private, VPC/KMS, TTFT, pilot success metrics.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in. Quick intro — I'm Samir, AE on the account, with Lena from the SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Elliot: Good thanks, thanks for making time. We've got a short agenda, wanna figure out the fastest way to get a prototype into our design editor.
[00:11] Samir: Perfect. High level: we typically offer a PLG/self-serve path with free credits to get you to the first token, and then if you hit production or need guarantees you can move to Dedicated or Private.
[00:20] Priya: So key for us is TTFT — time-to-first-token — and also the latency profile. The design editor is interactive, users expect sub 200 milliseconds ideally.
[00:30] Lena: Got it. For interactive UIs we usually recommend starting on Hosted for speed, we can show you batching knobs and prefix caching to reduce token cost without blowing latency.
[00:40] Marco: Quick question — our product handles some PII design assets, so we need to know about data residency and key management, we may need VPC access in about three months.
[00:49] Samir: Totally. We see that a lot — start on Hosted to iterate, then plan a Dedicated or Private (VPC) move. We support KMS integration and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; Dedicated can be configured with stricter retention and network controls.
[01:02] Elliot: Can you outline what the actual onboarding looks like for the PLG flow — like, we sign up and get credits and then what?
[01:08] Samir: You sign up, we provision evaluation credits — for example $5k — which you can use against our Hosted API. Lena will show the quickstart scripts: curl/SDK examples, a small benchmark harness, and a sample prompt set to validate quality. Most teams hit first token in under an hour if they have API keys and test payloads.
[01:24] Priya: Under an hour is great. But when you say "hit first token in under an hour", does that include us integrating into our app and doing an actual end-to-end?
[01:34] Lena: Good point. The raw API call and a playground test is quick; integrating into your app/UI depends on your dev cycle. We provide a small SDK snippet and templates for common stacks (Node/python). For an embedded iframe or web-client we usually see TTFT in 2–3 hours if you have a dev on it.
[01:50] Marco: On the compliance front, do you have SOC 2 and certs? Also SSO for team access.
[01:55] Samir: Yes, we publish SOC 2 reports, SAML/SSO for enterprise. Lena will attach the security pack after this call. For on-prem or VPC Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
[02:07] Priya: Great — can you confirm whether KV cache support is available? We want to do prefix caching for repeated prompts so we don't blow tokens.
[02:14] Lena: Yes, we support prefix/KV cache behaviors; our runtime manages KV cache for faster replays and lower cost. Note sometimes the auto-transcription writes that as "KV cash" — sorry i was reading notes — but yes it's KV cache.
[02:25] Elliot: We're evaluating cost vs latency. Our design flows are token heavy for some operations (image meta and long context), how do you recommend quantization or model choices?
[02:33] Lena: For heavy token workloads we recommend a mid-sized model with int8 quantization for cost savings and minimal latency hit. Redwood Optimize can give model/quantization suggestions based on sample payloads. For interactive tight SLOs we sometimes recommend Dedicated capacity pinned to a high-priority pool to avoid cold-start latencies.
[02:52] Marco: Any public perf numbers we can use as a baseline?
[02:55] Samir: We have model catalogs with benchmark profiles — I'll share the links. But as a rule of thumb: hosted smaller models can hit 80–160ms p50 on modern GPUs depending on sequence length; p95 varies. If you need guaranteed p95 SLAs, Dedicated is the right path.
[03:12] Priya: If we do an initial hosted pilot, what's the typical pilot scope? Two weeks?
[03:17] Lena: Two weeks is common: ingest sample prompts, run the benchmark harness, validate latency and cost per call, and monitor quality regressions. We provide tracing hooks and example dashboards so you can see per-route token breakdowns.
[03:28] Priya: Awesome. For the tech deep dive — Priya: what I want to validate is batching behavior for short interactive calls, how KV cache is managed across user sessions, and the route for pinning model versions.
[03:40] Lena: We'll cover batching and continuous batching heuristics, KV cache TTLs, and can demo rollouts and model pinning in the console.
[03:48] Elliot: I have an internal stakeholder who is worried about vendor lock-in and lock-in for the model. How easy is migration if we move from Hosted to Private?
[03:56] Samir: Our API is consistent across hosting modes; you can pin model versions and export configs. Private deploys require a bit of ops work but we provide an on-prem package and migration runbook. Customers typically do a staged migration: Hosted → Dedicated (reserved) → Private/VPC.
[04:12] Marco: For Dedicated, what are the commit terms and burst capacity options?
[04:18] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits. There's configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; we can propose a PO depending on your throughput forecast. We'll flag that in pricing.
[04:27] Priya: Regarding security, how are logs handled if we host on Redwood? We need audit logs and traceability for compliance.
[04:34] Lena: Hosted retains request/response logs per your plan — we can redact payloads or not store them; audit logs and token-level breakdowns are available. For strict compliance, Private with KMS is preferred.
[04:44] Elliot: Ok, can we talk specifics about the demo harness? We're going to run two scenarios: 1) micro-interactions for UI latency, 2) batch rewriters for longer prompts — want to see both cost and latency.
[04:55] Lena: That's a great split. We'll share a small harness with two scripts: a rapid-fire interactive runner that simulates 100 users with 200ms think times, and a batch runner for long-context rewriters. That should give you immediate comparative metrics.
[05:08] Marco: Any gotchas we should know when instrumenting metrics? E.g., token counting mismatches or prompt truncation.
[05:14] Lena: Watch for tokenization differences across model families, and watch for prefix caching effects — sometimes warm cached contexts look much cheaper. We'll include a note about tokenizer parity in the harness.
[05:24] Priya: We're also running internal evals for hallucination rates. Does Redwood provide eval tooling or integration to flag quality regressions?
[05:31] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval tracking and regression alerts tied to prompt sets, you can upload test prompts and get quality metrics. We'll include a short guide on integrating that.
[05:42] Elliot: How do we instrument SSO? We use Okta, want SSO and RBAC so only certain teams can create keys.
[05:49] Samir: Support for SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC exists. We'll send the SSO integration doc.
[05:55] Marco: For data residency — we host in us-east but need EU region soon; you support region pinning?
[06:02] Lena: Yes, region routing is supported — requests can be routed by region/policy; Private can be in specific cloud regions or on-prem.
[06:09] Priya: If we want an early look at model quality, can you recommend a model from your catalog?
[06:13] Lena: For design assistant style tasks we recommend a model tuned for instruction following and structured output; I'll send two options with perf/cost tradeoffs. Also include quantized variants.
[06:22] Elliot: About costs: our CFO will ask about unit economics — is there an easy way to show token-level cost including caching savings?
[06:29] Samir: In the console you get token-level cost breakdowns and prefix caching savings; we can export a sample cost sheet based on your sample runs.
[06:36] Priya: Ok — what happens if we exceed credits during the pilot? Billing or throttling?
[06:41] Samir: You can set quotas; by default we alert and then block if unpaid. For pilots we usually monitor and alert before you hit limits.
[06:50] Marco: Are there any limits on model variants during evaluation? We may want to try 3–4 variants quickly.
[06:55] Lena: No hard limits on variants; the catalog has curated models and you can request onboarding of community models if needed.
[07:02] Elliot: Let's talk timeline: We'd like to have the pilot started next week and a decision within ~3 weeks.
[07:08] Samir: Sounds feasible. I'll provision evaluation credits today and send invites. Lena will coordinate the 60–90 minute deep-dive early next week.
[07:15] Priya: For the deep dive can we do a quick run of the harness with one of our sample payloads so we can see a real trace?
[07:22] Lena: Yes, bring a sanitized sample and we'll run live. If you can't sanitize, we can run local harness with masked tokens.
[07:30] Elliot: One blocker — our security team will want SOC2, data flow diagrams, and proof of KMS integration options.
[07:36] Samir: We'll attach the SOC2 and the architecture docs. For KMS there's a standard integration spec and an on-prem/HSM note.
[07:44] Marco: On the migration path, will logs be accessible if we move to Private? We need full raw logs for debugging.
[07:50] Lena: In Private you can control retention and have direct access to logs; we can run a runbook to export historical logs if needed.
[07:57] Priya: Any performance tuning you recommend for our use case?
[08:01] Lena: Tune batch sizes conservatively for interactive calls, use continuous batching with small max latency windows. Also enable KV cache for repeated prompts, and run Optimize to pick a quantized model.
[08:12] Elliot: Ok great. I'm hearing a clear path: Hosted pilot now -> evaluate latency/cost and quality -> consider Dedicated or Private if we need stricter controls.
[08:21] Samir: Exactly.
[08:25] Marco: Before we wrap, is there a suggested checklist we can use to start the pilot?
[08:30] Lena: Yes: 1) Provide sample payloads and expected SLOs; 2) Get evaluation credits and account invites; 3) Run interactive harness and batch harness; 4) Share results and tune model/batching; 5) Decide on deployment mode. We'll send a one-page checklist.
[08:45] Priya: That sounds helpful.
[08:49] Samir: Awesome. Any final questions?
[08:52] Elliot: None from me, thanks.
[08:54] Marco: No, all good.
[08:56] Priya: Quick one — can you include an example of how RBAC is mapped to API keys?
[09:01] Lena: Yep, we'll include a sample mapping and the policy controls.
[09:05] Samir: Great. Recap of next steps: I'll provision $5k credits and send invites by tomorrow, Lena will share the security pack and schedule the SE deep-dive, Priya will share sample payloads. We'll run a 2-week hosted pilot starting when you confirm.
[09:20] Elliot: Thanks everyone, chat soon.
[09:23] End of recording.
